commit_message:
[HAL] Add command buffer flush and invalidate operations (#24945)

This PR adds HAL and runtime plumbing for ordered command-buffer buffer
flush and invalidate operations.

It introduces:

* `hal.command_buffer.flush_buffer`
* `hal.command_buffer.invalidate_buffer`
* HAL-to-VM lowering and VM imports
* runtime command-buffer API and vtable hooks
* VM module/shim plumbing
* inline command-buffer support
* deferred command-buffer recording/replay support
* HAL IR and HAL-to-VM test coverage

The operations carry a buffer reference, offset, and length and are
intended to represent execution-ordered cache maintenance for shared
non-coherent memory.

Stream-to-HAL lowering is intentionally left unchanged in this PR. Some
backends, especially Vulkan, require queue/submission-level handling to
preserve execution-time ordering because a HAL command buffer is
currently replayed into a single native `VkCommandBuffer`. Enabling
Stream lowering before that backend support exists could cause
unsupported runtime paths.

This PR therefore focuses on establishing the HAL/runtime infrastructure
first. Backend-specific execution support and Stream lowering can follow
separately.

Related to #24930.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward temporary DPS output copies (#24727)

Destination-passing-style (DPS) operations update explicit init
operands. After tensor-to-memref bufferization preserves tensor value
semantics, an update of a dispatch output may be represented by a
private temporary:

  %temp = memref.alloc()
  memref.copy %source, %temp
  linalg.generic ... outs(%temp)
  memref.copy %temp, %target

Forward the final target through this chain:

  memref.copy %source, %target
  linalg.generic ... outs(%target)

This removes the private allocation and copy-out. The copy-in is
redirected to %target rather than removed because the DPS operation may
still read its init operand.

Reject the rewrite when the copy source or another DPS operand may alias
the final target, or when an intervening operation may access that
target. These checks prevent moving target writes ahead of reads that
observed its previous contents.

MLIR alias analysis handles ordinary local values but does not
distinguish all IREE storage roots. Refine it with dispatch ABI facts:
different HAL interface binding ordinals and different memref global
symbols are disjoint; subspans of the same binding may overlap because
their byte offsets can be dynamic; and local allocations are disjoint
from bindings and globals. Unknown roots remain conservative.

Run the pass after bufferization has made the allocation and copies
explicit and before Linalg/LinalgExt lowering removes the DPS init
operands needed to retarget the operation.

---------

Signed-off-by: Hao Ren <rhao8608@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Yuwei Sun <yuweis2@illinois.edu>
name: linux_x64_gcc

commit_message:
[Torch] Register RestructureNonConstantAxes in the Torch input pipeline

RestructureNonConstantAxes already exists in torch-mlir but is not scheduled
by IREE's Torch input conversion pipeline
(compiler/plugins/input/Torch/InputConversion/Passes.cpp). As a result, ONNX
reductions with a runtime axes tensor (opset>=13, e.g. onnx.ReduceSum with
keepdims=1) keep a runtime `dim` on aten.sum.dim_IntList and fail to legalize
in ConvertTorchToLinalg:

    error: failed to legalize operation 'torch.aten.sum.dim_IntList'

This registers the existing pass right before ConvertTorchToTMTensor, so the
runtime axis is statically resolved (reshaped to a fixed axis) before the
Torch->Linalg conversions. No pass logic is added or modified.

Enabling this already-present pass flips 28 onnx_ops reduce cases from FAILED
to PASS (864 -> 892) in the cpu_llvm_sync config. This change is self-contained
and does not depend on any in-flight torch-mlir change.

Related to iree-org/iree#24378

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward temporary DPS output copies (#24727)

Destination-passing-style (DPS) operations update explicit init
operands. After tensor-to-memref bufferization preserves tensor value
semantics, an update of a dispatch output may be represented by a
private temporary:

  %temp = memref.alloc()
  memref.copy %source, %temp
  linalg.generic ... outs(%temp)
  memref.copy %temp, %target

Forward the final target through this chain:

  memref.copy %source, %target
  linalg.generic ... outs(%target)

This removes the private allocation and copy-out. The copy-in is
redirected to %target rather than removed because the DPS operation may
still read its init operand.

Reject the rewrite when the copy source or another DPS operand may alias
the final target, or when an intervening operation may access that
target. These checks prevent moving target writes ahead of reads that
observed its previous contents.

MLIR alias analysis handles ordinary local values but does not
distinguish all IREE storage roots. Refine it with dispatch ABI facts:
different HAL interface binding ordinals and different memref global
symbols are disjoint; subspans of the same binding may overlap because
their byte offsets can be dynamic; and local allocations are disjoint
from bindings and globals. Unknown roots remain conservative.

Run the pass after bufferization has made the allocation and copies
explicit and before Linalg/LinalgExt lowering removes the DPS init
operands needed to retarget the operation.

Signed-off-by: Hao Ren <rhao8608@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Yuwei Sun <yuweis2@illinois.edu>

commit_message:
[Stream] Make "consolidate" mode of SplitParameterEncoding actually consolidate

Fixes iree-org/iree#24920. By design, the `includeUnmodified=true` ("consolidate")
setting should move all parameters out of the main module, including the ones that
are still bound to be encoded online. However, the pass design was preventing this
from happening: `includeUnmodified` wasn't looked at and "raw" weights weren't
considered when filtering out the encoding computations deemed "hoistable" and
assigning encoder module locations to those.

The new approach is:
- hoist the chosen encoding computations into a temporary block and eliminate the
dead parameters from the main module;
- in "consolidate" mode, we can now claim unmodified parameters into the encoder
module as well;
- final serialization and DCE.

The change was assisted by Codex.

Signed-off-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>

Fixes iree-org/iree#24920. By design, the `includeUnmodified=true` ("consolidate")
setting should move all parameters out of the main module, including the ones that
are still bound to be encoded online. However, the pass design was preventing this
from happening: `includeUnmodified` wasn't looked at and "raw" weights weren't
considered when filtering out the encoding computations deemed "hoistable" and
assigning encoder module locations to those.

The new approach is:
- hoist the chosen encoding computations into a temporary block and eliminate the
dead parameters from the main module;
- in "consolidate" mode, we can now claim unmodified parameters into the encoder
module as well;
- final serialization and DCE.

The change was assisted by Codex.

Signed-off-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>
name: runtime :: windows-2022

commit_message:
[Stream] Make "consolidate" mode of SplitParameterEncoding actually consolidate

Fixes iree-org/iree#24920. By design, the `includeUnmodified=true` ("consolidate")
setting should move all parameters out of the main module, including the ones that
are still bound to be encoded online. However, the pass design was preventing this
from happening: `includeUnmodified` wasn't looked at and "raw" weights weren't
considered when filtering out the encoding computations deemed "hoistable" and
assigning encoder module locations to those.

The new approach is:
- hoist the chosen encoding computations into a temporary block and eliminate the
dead parameters from the main module;
- in "consolidate" mode, we can now claim unmodified parameters into the encoder
module as well;
- final serialization and DCE.

The change was assisted by Codex.

Signed-off-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Codegen] Compare binding ordinals only within one pipeline layout

A binding ordinal is an index into the binding list of a specific pipeline
layout, so ordinals from two different layouts describe unrelated positions.
mayAlias compared them anyway and reported binding(0) of one layout and
binding(1) of another as disjoint.

Two subspans reach the ordinal comparison whenever both operands resolve to a
binding, so the case never fell through to the AliasAnalysis fallback. Treat
differing layouts as may-alias and record the case in the table.

[Codegen] Compare binding ordinals only within one pipeline layout

A binding ordinal is an index into the binding list of a specific pipeline
layout, so ordinals from two different layouts describe unrelated positions.
mayAlias compared them anyway and reported binding(0) of one layout and
binding(1) of another as disjoint.

Two subspans reach the ordinal comparison whenever both operands resolve to a
binding, so the case never fell through to the AliasAnalysis fallback. Treat
differing layouts as may-alias and record the case in the table.

Signed-off-by: Hao Ren <rhao8608@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[HAL] Add command buffer flush and invalidate operations (#24945)

This PR adds HAL and runtime plumbing for ordered command-buffer buffer
flush and invalidate operations.

It introduces:

* `hal.command_buffer.flush_buffer`
* `hal.command_buffer.invalidate_buffer`
* HAL-to-VM lowering and VM imports
* runtime command-buffer API and vtable hooks
* VM module/shim plumbing
* inline command-buffer support
* deferred command-buffer recording/replay support
* HAL IR and HAL-to-VM test coverage

The operations carry a buffer reference, offset, and length and are
intended to represent execution-ordered cache maintenance for shared
non-coherent memory.

Stream-to-HAL lowering is intentionally left unchanged in this PR. Some
backends, especially Vulkan, require queue/submission-level handling to
preserve execution-time ordering because a HAL command buffer is
currently replayed into a single native `VkCommandBuffer`. Enabling
Stream lowering before that backend support exists could cause
unsupported runtime paths.

This PR therefore focuses on establishing the HAL/runtime infrastructure
first. Backend-specific execution support and Stream lowering can follow
separately.

Related to #24930.

commit_message:
[HAL] Add command buffer flush and invalidate operations (#24945)

This PR adds HAL and runtime plumbing for ordered command-buffer buffer
flush and invalidate operations.

It introduces:

* `hal.command_buffer.flush_buffer`
* `hal.command_buffer.invalidate_buffer`
* HAL-to-VM lowering and VM imports
* runtime command-buffer API and vtable hooks
* VM module/shim plumbing
* inline command-buffer support
* deferred command-buffer recording/replay support
* HAL IR and HAL-to-VM test coverage

The operations carry a buffer reference, offset, and length and are
intended to represent execution-ordered cache maintenance for shared
non-coherent memory.

Stream-to-HAL lowering is intentionally left unchanged in this PR. Some
backends, especially Vulkan, require queue/submission-level handling to
preserve execution-time ordering because a HAL command buffer is
currently replayed into a single native `VkCommandBuffer`. Enabling
Stream lowering before that backend support exists could cause
unsupported runtime paths.

This PR therefore focuses on establishing the HAL/runtime infrastructure
first. Backend-specific execution support and Stream lowering can follow
separately.

Related to #24930.

commit_message:
[Vulkan] Accept foreign semaphores in queue operations (#25010)

Queue operations rejected any semaphore not created by the same Vulkan
device with UNIMPLEMENTED. Use host deferral instead.

---------

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert PT2E per-token quantization to LinalgExt

Convert quantized_decomposed.quantize_per_token and dequantize_per_token
to iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine and dequantize_affine. As in
torchao's PerToken granularity, the block size is one along every input
dimension but the last, which each block spans, so the parameters are
indexed by the leading dimensions and the data path needs no reshape.
The unit last dimension that PT2E keeps in the parameters is dropped
like any other static unit dimension.

Per-token needs no reshape, so only the checks shared with the other
granularities apply.

Quantization computes in the scale type, f64 for the scales that
torch.ao computes per token, as the per-token reference does.
Dequantization matches the PT2E reference. The per-token reference adds
the zero point before rounding, so quantize ties with odd zero points
differ from it and from the Torch-to-Linalg lowering, which follows it.

Depends on the torch-mlir ops from llvm/torch-mlir#4765.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

Convert quantized_decomposed.quantize_per_token and dequantize_per_token
to iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine and dequantize_affine. As in
torchao's PerToken granularity, the block size is one along every input
dimension but the last, which each block spans, so the parameters are
indexed by the leading dimensions and the data path needs no reshape.
The unit last dimension that PT2E keeps in the parameters is dropped
like any other static unit dimension.

Per-token needs no reshape, so only the checks shared with the other
granularities apply.

Quantization computes in the scale type, f64 for the scales that
torch.ao computes per token, as the per-token reference does.
Dequantization matches the PT2E reference. The per-token reference adds
the zero point before rounding, so quantize ties with odd zero points
differ from it and from the Torch-to-Linalg lowering, which follows it.

Depends on the torch-mlir ops from llvm/torch-mlir#4765.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
name: linux_arm64_clang

Queue operations rejected any semaphore not created by the same Vulkan
device with UNIMPLEMENTED. Use host deferral instead.

---------

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@6be022066fd2

Adapted to change of ROCDL "wave per eu" attributes type from int to string in LLVM commit
4d5db577f969 [mlir][ROCDL][AMDGPU] Support string waves_per_eu for min,max occupancy range (#225663)

The TOSA compliance table has grown beyond what MSVC can support on the stack.
Apparently, the function size / stack size has been an issue before, see e.g.:
9e69e851a1f8 [NFC][mlir][tosa] Use optnone for compliance initialization under ASan (#229292)
1e9bc138d8f3 [mlir][Tosa] Optimize compliance initialization for size to improve build time (NFC) (#222791)
This change currently adds an experimental mitigation by splitting up the initialization.

Claude Code has been used to find the LLVM commits related to the issued and adapt the IREE side code. The changes have been reviewed manually.

Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward temporary DPS output copies (#24727)

Destination-passing-style (DPS) operations update explicit init
operands. After tensor-to-memref bufferization preserves tensor value
semantics, an update of a dispatch output may be represented by a
private temporary:

  %temp = memref.alloc()
  memref.copy %source, %temp
  linalg.generic ... outs(%temp)
  memref.copy %temp, %target

Forward the final target through this chain:

  memref.copy %source, %target
  linalg.generic ... outs(%target)

This removes the private allocation and copy-out. The copy-in is
redirected to %target rather than removed because the DPS operation may
still read its init operand.

Reject the rewrite when the copy source or another DPS operand may alias
the final target, or when an intervening operation may access that
target. These checks prevent moving target writes ahead of reads that
observed its previous contents.

MLIR alias analysis handles ordinary local values but does not
distinguish all IREE storage roots. Refine it with dispatch ABI facts:
different HAL interface binding ordinals and different memref global
symbols are disjoint; subspans of the same binding may overlap because
their byte offsets can be dynamic; and local allocations are disjoint
from bindings and globals. Unknown roots remain conservative.

Run the pass after bufferization has made the allocation and copies
explicit and before Linalg/LinalgExt lowering removes the DPS init
operands needed to retarget the operation.

---------

Signed-off-by: Hao Ren <rhao8608@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Yuwei Sun <yuweis2@illinois.edu>

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward temporary DPS output copies (#24727)

Destination-passing-style (DPS) operations update explicit init
operands. After tensor-to-memref bufferization preserves tensor value
semantics, an update of a dispatch output may be represented by a
private temporary:

  %temp = memref.alloc()
  memref.copy %source, %temp
  linalg.generic ... outs(%temp)
  memref.copy %temp, %target

Forward the final target through this chain:

  memref.copy %source, %target
  linalg.generic ... outs(%target)

This removes the private allocation and copy-out. The copy-in is
redirected to %target rather than removed because the DPS operation may
still read its init operand.

Reject the rewrite when the copy source or another DPS operand may alias
the final target, or when an intervening operation may access that
target. These checks prevent moving target writes ahead of reads that
observed its previous contents.

MLIR alias analysis handles ordinary local values but does not
distinguish all IREE storage roots. Refine it with dispatch ABI facts:
different HAL interface binding ordinals and different memref global
symbols are disjoint; subspans of the same binding may overlap because
their byte offsets can be dynamic; and local allocations are disjoint
from bindings and globals. Unknown roots remain conservative.

Run the pass after bufferization has made the allocation and copies
explicit and before Linalg/LinalgExt lowering removes the DPS init
operands needed to retarget the operation.

---------

Signed-off-by: Yuwei Sun <yuweis2@illinois.edu>
Signed-off-by: Hao Ren <rhao8608@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Yuwei Sun <yuweis2@illinois.edu>

commit_message:
[Torch] Preserve PT2E per-channel-group quantization as LinalgExt ops (#25008)

Extends `ConvertTorchQuantizationToLinalgExt` to the PT2E
`quantized_decomposed` per-channel-group quantize/dequantize ops. All
granularities, including per-tensor and per-channel, derive their layout
from a torchao-style block size and share one operand check. Bool zero
points are treated as unsigned.

Part of #24862.

---------

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>

[Torch] Preserve PT2E per-channel-group quantization as LinalgExt ops (#25008)

Extends `ConvertTorchQuantizationToLinalgExt` to the PT2E
`quantized_decomposed` per-channel-group quantize/dequantize ops. All
granularities, including per-tensor and per-channel, derive their layout
from a torchao-style block size and share one operand check. Bool zero
points are treated as unsigned.

Part of #24862.

---------

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
name: linux_arm64_clang

commit_message:
[Integrate] Update torch-mlir to 201b80fb

Update to upstream torch-mlir through 201b80fb, using the IREE
integration revision adapted to the current LLVM pin.

The new range lowers ONNX QuantizeLinear and DequantizeLinear to
quantized_decomposed ops, which fixes test_quantizelinear_axis, so drop
it from the expected compile failures of the CI-exercised configs.

test_dequantizelinear_uint16 now fails to compile. The new
DequantizeLinear conversion accepts only a fixed list of storage dtypes,
which excludes uint16 until Torch::getScalarTypeForType can map it, so
onnx.DequantizeLinear stays unconverted. Mark it as an expected compile
failure until the conversion supports uint16.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
Keep equal elements in order when lowering sort to loops

The scalar bubble sort for iree_linalg_ext.sort swapped adjacent
elements whenever the comparator returned false, which includes
elements that compare equal. With a strict comparator such as LT, this
reversed the order of equal keys, so `stablehlo.sort` with
`is_stable = true` returned their payloads out of order.

Also evaluate the comparator with swapped operands and only swap when
the right element is strictly ordered before the left one. The sorting
pass in TopkV2Op shares the sweep helper and keeps its current behavior.

Assisted-by: Codex / gpt-6.1-sol

commit_message:
[Codegen] Add bufferization support for CastToRaggedShapeOp and LinearizeRaggedDimsOp (#24193)

This is PR 4/N of landing block sparse changes that are captured in this
branch :


https://github.com/MaheshRavishankar/iree/tree/users/MaheshRavishankar/blockSparseCommits

Adds `BufferizableOpInterfac`e external models for two tensor-ext ops
that describe ragged shapes:
- `iree_tensor_ext.cast_to_ragged_shape` — reinterprets a source buffer
as a rank-(n+1) ragged buffer by
attaching a RaggedShapeAttr as the memref layout.
-`iree_tensor_ext.linearize_ragged_dims` — the inverse view: collapses
the ragged dimensions of a source
buffer back into a single dense dimension and drops the ragged layout.
  
Both ops are pure views, so the interface implementations:
- Report the operands as reads and never as writes (including
`resultBufferizesToMemoryWrite = false`).
- Set `mustBufferizeInPlace = true` and mark the result as
`BufferRelation::Equivalent` to source, so
bufferization does not introduce a copy.
- For `cast_to_ragged_shape`, the result memref's layout is the ragged
encoding promoted from the tensor
encoding; operand buffers use the identity layout.
- For `linearize_ragged_dims`, both operand and result memrefs use the
identity layout; the result simply
drops the ragged encoding.
`bufferize` replaces the tensor-typed op with an identical memref-typed
version of itself — no data is
moved.

[Codegen] Add bufferization support for CastToRaggedShapeOp and LinearizeRaggedDimsOp (#24193)

This is PR 4/N of landing block sparse changes that are captured in this
branch :


https://github.com/MaheshRavishankar/iree/tree/users/MaheshRavishankar/blockSparseCommits

Adds `BufferizableOpInterfac`e external models for two tensor-ext ops
that describe ragged shapes:
- `iree_tensor_ext.cast_to_ragged_shape` — reinterprets a source buffer
as a rank-(n+1) ragged buffer by
attaching a RaggedShapeAttr as the memref layout.
-`iree_tensor_ext.linearize_ragged_dims` — the inverse view: collapses
the ragged dimensions of a source
buffer back into a single dense dimension and drops the ragged layout.
  
Both ops are pure views, so the interface implementations:
- Report the operands as reads and never as writes (including
`resultBufferizesToMemoryWrite = false`).
- Set `mustBufferizeInPlace = true` and mark the result as
`BufferRelation::Equivalent` to source, so
bufferization does not introduce a copy.
- For `cast_to_ragged_shape`, the result memref's layout is the ragged
encoding promoted from the tensor
encoding; operand buffers use the identity layout.
- For `linearize_ragged_dims`, both operand and result memrefs use the
identity layout; the result simply
drops the ragged encoding.
`bufferize` replaces the tensor-typed op with an identical memref-typed
version of itself — no data is
moved.
